Extend the provided multi-file CPU packet-scheduling library into a branchable experiment engine.
Work in `/workspace/submission`; packet, policy, scheduler and ordered-storage modules are provided.
The entry is `python3 -I -B submission/cli.py`, reading one JSON batch through EOF.
Return the complete event log and final state certificate specified in `PROTOCOL.md`.
Preserve locally sorted PIFOs, staged input FIFOs, byte limits and fixed cyclic service opportunities.
Add cancellation, live lag accounting, conservative counter migration, and isolated save/restore branches.
Policy ranks, admission failures, refill pushout and automatic sampling must remain causally consistent.
Reconfiguration changes future classification and counters without relocating resident packets.
Checkpoint restore recovers the entire computational state without rewinding the output log.
The domain includes large backlogs and frequent branches; repeated whole-backlog work is costly.
All ordering, arithmetic, observable boundaries and whole-batch work limits are in `PROTOCOL.md`.
Complete the experiment adapter and repair/extend the existing computational modules as needed.
You may reorganize modules and add ordinary supporting files; equivalent implementations are accepted.
Submit the complete `submission/` directory, including a standalone UTF-8 `cli.py` entry.
The environment is offline Python 3.11.14, its standard library and the supplied local modules.
No external package, service, trace download, GPU or physical switch is required.
Run `python3 check.py submission` for the public sanity examples.
Execution limits, child I/O, syscall policy and writable storage are in `RESOURCES.md`.
The baseline is runnable as a library; its extended experiment adapter is unfinished.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
Everything is complete and validated. Final summary of the implementation:

**`submission/cli.py`** â entry point: one UTF-8 JSON request through EOF, strict `{"error":"invalid"}` for bad UTF-8 / malformed JSON / duplicate keys at any depth / nonfinite values (`1e999`) / trailing values, always exit zero, compact JSON out.

**`submission/packet.py`** â `Pkt` with the immutable tie ordinal (= event index; the baseline wrongly used the flow id) plus its immutable staging slot for O(1) cancellation.

**`submission/algorithms.py`** â FIFO / SP / SFF / WFQ with exact integer finish tags `max(F,V)+ceil(lengthÂ·2Â²â°/weight)` (replacing the baseline's float division), rank advance on rejected attempts, weight updates affecting future attempts only, copy-on-write flow tables, and sorted certificate tables.

**`submission/treap.py`** â ordered storage: versioned copy-on-write treaps (lean for bank PIFOs, fat for the global live set with subtree sizes and *lazy lag accounting*), so "every remaining strictly lower-rank resident gains one lag" plus rank_error is a single O(depth) descent instead of a backlog walk, and a checkpoint is one root reference.

**`submission/scheduler.py`** â fixed cyclic opportunities, argmin bank routing with the initial stagger bias, refill-then-longest-prefix pushout in descending key order, serve-frees-bytes-before-refill, post-pop refill, sampling (X before normalization, row translation by min over q, `H=floor(H/2)+X`), automatic samples after the triggering enqueue, prefix-quantized counter migration, cancellation, and isolated save/restore branches with the name registry outside saved state. Staging FIFOs are chunked so checkpoints never copy a backlog.

**`submission/utils.py`** â the experiment adapter; **`sortedcontainers/`** â the provided helper kept for the baseline API.
